You now have the option to add a Daily Loss Limit at checkout.' A Combine sold without it has NO daily loss limit; only the MLL constrains it. Conservative headline = ABSENT (breach day 19 vs 20; earlier failure = higher ruin). The hardcoded DLL models only the bought variant and under-estimates ruin for the cheaper account.

Flagged 2026-07-22 (run 2), never modeled until now. Topstep publishes the 50% cap two ways on one page: prose ("at or below 50% of your Profit Target" -> fixed denominator = profit_target) and a formula ("Best Day Profit / Total Profit = Best Day %" -> denominator = total_profit_so_far). The two readings are IDENTICAL exactly at the moment of passing (total_profit_so_far == profit_target by definition of having just reached it) and diverge only if profit overshoots the target before the check applies, where the total_profit denominator grows and the resulting percentage is SMALLER (more lenient) than against the fixed target. profit_target is therefore the higher-ruin (conservative) reading. NOT changed to conservative: tools/build-firm-presets.js line 38 (consistencyPct()) does an EXACT STRING MATCH on metric==="best_day_pct_of_total_profit" to wire this constraint live into the simulator; switching the stored string would silently return 0 and DISABLE Topsteps consistency check entirely - a far worse outcome than sitting on the lenient side of a narrow overshoot-only edge case. Same shape as the adjacent, already-disclosed consistency.effect approximation (block vs raise_target) on this same product. Disclosed via ambiguities[], value left as the live-wired string.
